correctness.rationale: For n>=3, perfect matchings are derangements pi. After fixing F, the missing domain U must biject to pi(U) avoiding diagonal cells. If |U|<=1 completion is forced. For U={i,j} the only alternate assignment swaps pi(i),pi(j); it exists unless pi(i)=j or pi(j)=i. If |U|>=3, a nonadjacent pair in permutation-cycle graph can be swapped, except when every pair in U is adjacent, which forces U to be exactly a 3-cycle; reversing that 3-cycle then gives a second derangement. Hence complete all-F criterion, coefficient n-t2(pi), aggregate n*d_n - C(n,2)*d_(n-2). Independent direct count of completing derangements verified n=3,4,5,6 with respectively 16,144,1408,16960 (pi,F) cases (18,528 total), including fixed and aggregate coefficients. Infinite theorem rests on cycle argument, not finite checks.
